alex: Quick sync — trying to repro the ~2–3% nightly perf regression. My hypothesis: kernel-selector + batching window interaction when KV cache/multi-step requests are hit. Replay harness vs synthetic load produce different batch windows and we end up selecting different kernels. Can we converge on an apples-to-apples run?
jessie: Yep. I noticed on one host with driver 530 the selector picked tensorcore fp16 kernels, on 525 it fell back to a bf16 path. Snippet from logs: `selected_kernel: matmul_tc_fp16 (latency_est 0.82ms)` vs `selected_kernel: matmul_bf16_opt (latency_est 1.05ms)`. :thinking:
maria: Actionable plan: run side-by-side on the same GPU type, same docker image, same CUDA and driver. Force batch_window to a fixed value for a smoke sweep (eg batch_window=16) and then sweep. Also try forcing `prefetch_kv=false` to see KV impact. Example run:```bash
DOCKER_TAG=ci-bench:2026-03-18-driver-530
docker run --gpus all -e BATCH_WINDOW=16 -e PREFETCH_KV=false $DOCKER_TAG 
./bench --replay /mnt/replay/trace.json --out /tmp/res.json
```
kai: We should capture microprofile traces (ncu or our bench profiler) and record per-kernel launch count + durations + bytes. Key metrics: kernel_launches_per_request, median_token_p99, kernel_selection_reason (batch_size, seq_len, quant). Also capture `nvml` driver version and `nvidia-smi` output in the run metadata.
deploy-bot: scheduled bench job `eng-runtime/regression-investigate/2087654321` on bench-cluster-5 at 2026-03-18T12:30:00Z :white_check_mark:
jessie: Another thing — KV cache behavior shortens active matmul seqlen on subsequent tokens, which nudges selector to a smaller-kernel path. That increases kernel launches and launch overhead becomes non-trivial. We should log `selected_kernel` per token (or per 8-token window) to see oscillation.
alex: Good point. Let's add a debug flag `--emit-selection-log=/tmp/selection.log` so the harness writes one line per token: `token_index,seq_len,selected_kernel,launch_time_us`. Then we can compute extra latency due to launches.
maria: Test matrix proposal (small, to start): GPUs=[A100-40GB, A10-24GB], Drivers=[525,530], CUDA=[11.8,12.1], ImageTags=[ci-bench:2026-03-18-driver-525, ci-bench:2026-03-18-driver-530], KernelFlags=[default, --disable-tc, --force-int8-path]. Run replay + synthetic: replay uses real client trace (seqlen dist), synthetic uses our generator with same seqlen histogram.
jessie: For the apples-to-apples synthetic, use the replay's seqlen histogram to drive generation (not fixed seqlen). That fixed a lot of earlier mismatches. Command to generate:```python
# synth_gen.py
hist = load_hist('/mnt/replay/seq_hist.json')
emit_synthetic(hist, rate=1000rps, out='synth.json')
```
kai: Perf collection checklist: - enable ncu sampling + cuda events - capture `nvprof --metrics` fallback - collect `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log` - pack container image manifest + sha - diff `selected_kernel` sequences between runs.
alex: If we isolate a regression to selector heuristics we can add a deterministic comparator: given seq_len distribution + batch_window, compute recommended kernel and compare to actually selected kernel. Fail if mismatch rate > 1%. That gives us a guard in CI.
maria: One more practical note: ensure kernel flags are identical in the image and at runtime (we saw a case where `/etc/modprobe.d` flags on host affected launch path even when container had updated libs). So capture `cat /etc/modprobe.d/*` in the run metadata.
jessie: I'll run the two-driver sweep tomorrow morning and upload traces to GCS under `gs://redwood-bench/regression-2087654321/`. Will notify here when done.
alex: Thanks — when you upload please include a tiny manifest `manifest.txt` with: driver, cuda, image_tag, gpu_model, bench_config, nvml_output, selection_log. Then we can script the comparer.
deploy-bot: job completed: eng-runtime/regression-investigate/2087654321 -> logs: gs://redwood-bench/regression-2087654321/run-001.tar.gz
maria: Ack — will start parsing. If anyone wants to join debugging session at 15:00 UTC ping me. :mag:
